clue.text: It's cooler to get on trumpet

parts.note: a fan is something that cools you
to fare is to get on, as in 'how did you get on?'

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a trumpet might chill the room.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trumpet' is a noun here: a flourish on brass instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A ceremonial blast on brass instruments is a flourish heard as trumpeting.

clue.text: See 16
Stuffed if overturning going round bend

indicators.note: going round tells us the turned word encloses the next piece
in a down clue overturning means the word if is read from the bottom up

parts.note: an arc is a bend or curve

explanation.surface: A stuffed thing tips over while going round a corner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overturning' reverses the two-letter word, and 'going round' makes that turned pair wrap the bend, one letter either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Farci is a French culinary term, adopted in English menus, meaning filled with stuffing.

clue.text: Mug on old jerk like a Dalek?

parts.note: to mug someone is to rob them
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: Someone attacks an old idiot, Dalek-style.
explanation.walkthrough: A Dalek is the mechanical-sounding alien from the British TV series Doctor Who; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Daleks move and speak mechanically, which is the quality of a machine or automaton.

clue.text: Why clad in tatters for the theatre?

indicators.note: in tatters means torn apart, so the letters of why clad are rearranged

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about why someone dresses in rags at the playhouse.
explanation.walkthrough: The ALDWYCH is a theatre in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: The Aldwych is a well-known West End playhouse, named after the street it stands on.

clue.text: She's after container for a jalopy

definitions.text: She's after container for a jalopy

parts.words: She's after container for a jalopy
parts.note: a girl's name which, following a word for a tin container, gives an old name for a ramshackle Ford car

explanation.surface: A woman goes looking for a box to hold an old banger.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'tin Lizzie' is the nickname of the Ford Model T, hence any old car; the girl's name comes after TIN, a container.
explanation.definitionFit: The name completes the nickname for a cheap old car, so the answer is the female name in that phrase.

clue.text: Idle rich lack such quality to broadcast with Whicker

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so the letters of to and Whicker are scattered

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: The leisured classes are said to lack a trait the TV reporter Alan Whicker broadcast about.
explanation.walkthrough: Alan Whicker was a British TV travel documentary presenter; 'with' is only a link here.
explanation.definitionFit: A belief in diligent labour is the quality the leisured idle rich are accused of lacking.

clue.text: Hair style of man with cleavage

parts.note: to man a ship is to crew it
a cleavage is a split or cut

explanation.surface: A hairdo belonging to a man showing a bit of cleavage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man' is a verb, to staff a vessel, not a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a very short cropped haircut, originally associated with rowing teams.

clue.text: See 16
Singers eschewing hard, ropey material

indicators.note: eschewing means avoiding, so the letter for hard is dropped

parts.note: a choir is a group of singers
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: Vocalists avoid a difficult, poor-quality fabric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ropey' means poor in British slang, but here it literally means suitable for rope.
explanation.definitionFit: Coir is coconut-husk fibre used for making rope and matting.

clue.text: Hitler's offensive, second-rate, Ritz-like development on top of Grossglockner

parts.note: B is a grade below A, so second-rate

indicators.note: development means changing form, so the letters of Ritz-like are reworked
top of means the first letter of Grossglockner

explanation.surface: A Nazi assault is described as a shabby, hotel-like building project atop an Austrian mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: The Grossglockner is Austria's highest mountain.
explanation.definitionFit: The blitzkrieg, or lightning war, was the rapid attack method used by Hitler's armies.

clue.text: Confession of Rex in dress

indicators.note: in tells us the letter for king goes inside the garment

parts.note: a shift is a simple straight dress
R stands for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A king's admission that he wears a dress.
explanation.walkthrough: As in 'short shrift', originally the brief confession given to a condemned prisoner.
explanation.definitionFit: Shrift is an archaic word for confession to a priest and the absolution that follows.

clue.text: Pressing need of way-out bloke two times removed to outskirts of city

indicators.note: removed means the two letters for time are taken away

parts.note: an exit is a way out
a gent is a bloke
T is the abbreviation for time, so two times is two Ts

indicators.note: outskirts means the first and last letters of city

explanation.surface: An eccentric man is twice banished to the edge of town out of urgent necessity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'way-out' looks like eccentric, but is a door out; 'removed' strips both Ts, and 'outskirts of' takes the first and last letters of city.
explanation.definitionFit: An exigency is an urgent demand or requirement arising from circumstances.

clue.text: Most supermarket food is supplied by agent carrying a gun around

indicators.note: around tells us the gun-carrying word wraps the agent

parts.note: packed is slang for carrying a gun
a rep is a sales agent

explanation.surface: Grocery shops are stocked by an armed salesman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supplied by' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Food that is wrapped before it reaches the shop is sold ready-wrapped in the packet.

clue.text: Birds inspiring short, short passage by broadcast poet

parts.note: para is a shortened form of paragraph, itself a short passage of text

indicators.note: broadcast means spoken on air, so we hear the poet's name

parts.note: John Keats was an English Romantic poet

explanation.surface: Birds inspire a brief radio reading by a poet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspiring' and 'by' are links; KEETS is how the Romantic poet's name sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Parakeets are small long-tailed parrots, a group of birds.

clue.text: Acknowledgement by a US officer, perhaps, of latest introduction to a good dining establishment, in Hardy's words?

definitions.text: Acknowledgement by a US officer, perhaps, of latest introduction to a good dining establishment, in Hardy's words?

parts.words: Acknowledgement by a US officer, perhaps, of latest introduction to a good dining establishment, in Hardy's words?
parts.note: read as an officer admitting he has been brought into yet ... excellent officers' canteen, using American phrasing; really Oliver Hardy's catchphrase to Stan Laurel

explanation.surface: An American officer remarks on being shown a nice new canteen, quoting the comedian Oliver Hardy.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'mess' is where officers eat, so a 'fine mess' is a good dining establishment; 'gotten' is the American touch.
explanation.definitionFit: This was Oliver Hardy's exasperated catchphrase to Stan Laurel in their comedy films.

clue.text: Flash author

explanation.definitionFit: The word means a tiny flash, and is also the surname of the novelist Muriel Spark.

clue.text: Programme that puts some of its audience on the line

definitions.text: Programme that puts some of its audience on the line

parts.words: Programme that puts some of its audience on the line
parts.note: a broadcast in which listeners call in by telephone and so are put on the line, not put at risk

explanation.surface: A show that endangers some of its viewers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the line' suggests at risk, but means on the telephone.
explanation.definitionFit: A radio or TV show where listeners ring in to speak on air takes calls from its audience.

clue.text: Act, or miss out fate of Big Brother contestant?

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters of act, or miss are rearranged

explanation.surface: Perform or vanish, as a reality TV housemate may.
explanation.walkthrough: Big Brother is a reality TV show in which housemates are voted out one by one.
explanation.definitionFit: Exclusion by the group is what happens to an evicted housemate, voted out of society.

clue.text: Views with which a letter might end

definitions.meaning: ... as a verb means looks at or considers

definitions.text: with which a letter might end
definitions.meaning: letters often close with best wishes

explanation.definitionFit: The word means looks at or considers, and is also a common sign-off wishing someone well.

clue.text: Behind about to turn less flexible

parts.note: the stern is the back or behind of a ship

indicators.note: to turn means the word for about is read backwards

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A rear end about to turn proves stiffer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to turn' reverses the short word for about; a ship's stern is its rear, hence behind.
explanation.definitionFit: Stern means strict and unyielding, so its comparative means more rigid.

clue.text: See 16
Maybe Robin Hood's type of music gets the girl round

parts.note: folk is a genre of music
her refers to a girl
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: An outlaw's favourite genre brings his sweetheart around.
explanation.walkthrough: 's is read as 'is', a link; 'gets' is a link too.
explanation.definitionFit: Robin Hood is a legendary popular champion, an example of a celebrated figure of folk tradition.

clue.text: See 16
Top of apple tart turned up in US city

indicators.note: in a down clue turned up means the letters are read from the bottom upwards
top of means the first letter of apple

parts.note: tart is slang for a promiscuous woman, a slut

explanation.surface: The crust of an apple pie flips over in an American town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' reverses A plus SLUT as a whole, giving the Oklahoma city.
explanation.definitionFit: Tulsa is a city in Oklahoma, in the United States.

clue.text: Pan's place at no time duplicated light

indicators.note: duplicated means the word is written twice

parts.note: never means at no time
to land is to alight, as a bird lights on a branch

explanation.surface: A god's home is never doubly illuminated.
explanation.walkthrough: Pan is Peter Pan, not the Greek god; 'light' is a verb, to settle.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the imaginary island where Peter Pan lives in J M Barrie's story.

clue.text: See 26
Like the universal store gets your head

parts.note: one's is the impersonal form of your
the top is the head of something

explanation.surface: A store selling everything gets your attention.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A shop where you can buy everything in a single visit offers everything at one place.

clue.text: Fred has a long look round one

indicators.note: round tells us the look encloses the numeral

parts.note: a stare is a long look
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Fred is given a lingering glance by someone.
explanation.walkthrough: Fred Astaire was the American dancer and film star.
explanation.definitionFit: The first name identifies the famous Hollywood dancer by surname.
